evals.name: OSSM 3.0 setup
evals.prompt: Set up OpenShift Service Mesh 3.0 for a production environment. Install the Red Hat operator (servicemeshoperator3 from redhat-operators), create an IstioCNI and Istio CR in istio-system with the openshift profile, enforce strict mTLS everywhere via PeerAuthentication, and enroll namespaces 'payments', 'orders', and 'notifications' into the mesh. Also install the Kiali operator for the dashboard.
expectations: Operator Subscription uses name: servicemeshoperator3 with source: redhat-operators
Output contains kind: IstioCNI with apiVersion: sailoperator.io/v1 and profile: openshift
Output contains kind: Istio with apiVersion: sailoperator.io/v1
Istio CR has profile: openshift and namespace: istio-system
IstioCNI is created before the Istio CR (correct install order)
Output contains kind: PeerAuthentication with spec.mtls.mode: STRICT
Namespaces payments, orders, and notifications have label istio-injection: enabled
Does NOT use ServiceMeshControlPlane or ServiceMeshMemberRoll (those are OSSM 2.x)
Kiali operator Subscription uses source: redhat-operators
Output includes verification commands (oc get pods, oc wait)

evals.name: Rollout + Istio canary traffic management
evals.prompt: Set up a canary rollout for 'payments-api' in the 'payments' namespace using Argo Rollouts with Istio for traffic management. The image is quay.io/acme/payments-api:v3.0.0 with 5 replicas. Canary steps: 10% traffic, pause 2 minutes, 30% with Prometheus analysis checking error rate < 1%, 60%, pause 5 minutes, then 100%. Create the Rollout, stable and canary Services, VirtualService, DestinationRule with stable and canary subsets, and an AnalysisTemplate that queries Prometheus at http://prometheus.istio-system:9090 for the istio_requests_total error rate. Show how the Rollouts controller automatically updates VirtualService weights during progression.
expectations: Output includes kind: Rollout with strategy.canary containing trafficRouting.istio
Rollout trafficRouting references the VirtualService by name and the stable/canary Services
Canary steps include setWeight 10, pause 2m, setWeight 30 with analysis, setWeight 60, pause 5m
Analysis step references an AnalysisTemplate by name
Output includes two Services: one for stable traffic and one for canary traffic
Both Services select the same app label but Rollouts manages the pod-template-hash selector
Output includes a VirtualService with route entries for stable and canary destinations with initial weights
Output includes a DestinationRule with two subsets (stable and canary) using pod-template-hash labels or matching labels
Output includes an AnalysisTemplate with Prometheus provider querying istio_requests_total for error rate
AnalysisTemplate has successCondition checking error rate < 0.01 or success rate >= 0.99
Explains that the Rollouts controller automatically updates VirtualService weights as canary progresses through steps
VirtualService and DestinationRule use networking.istio.io/v1 apiVersion

evals.name: Blue-green rollout with Istio traffic switching
evals.prompt: Set up a blue-green deployment for 'checkout-svc' in the 'checkout' namespace using Argo Rollouts with Istio. Active service 'checkout-active', preview service 'checkout-preview'. Do NOT auto-promote — require manual approval. Add a prePromotionAnalysis that checks the preview's error rate via Istio metrics (istio_requests_total) before allowing promotion. Configure the VirtualService to route all production traffic to active and a header-based rule (x-preview: true) to route to preview for testing. Generate Rollout, both Services, VirtualService, DestinationRule, and AnalysisTemplate.
expectations: Output includes kind: Rollout with strategy.blueGreen
Blue-green config has activeService and previewService references
autoPromotionEnabled is false for manual approval
prePromotionAnalysis references an AnalysisTemplate
Output includes two Services: checkout-active and checkout-preview
Output includes a VirtualService with default route to active service
VirtualService has a header-based match rule for x-preview: true routing to preview
Output includes a DestinationRule with subsets or host references for active and preview
AnalysisTemplate queries Prometheus using istio_requests_total for the preview service error rate
AnalysisTemplate successCondition checks error rate threshold
VirtualService and DestinationRule use networking.istio.io/v1
Explains the promotion flow: preview deployed → prePromotionAnalysis runs → manual promote → active switches

evals.name: Trade-off: canary vs blue-green for payments API
evals.prompt: We're deploying a payments API that processes credit card transactions. Downtime costs us $50k/hour. We need to validate new versions with real traffic but can't afford to expose more than 5% of users to a bad release. We also need the ability to test the new version with specific headers before any real user traffic hits it. Should we use canary or blue-green with Istio? Why? What are we giving up with your recommendation?
expectations: Recommends blue-green (not canary) as primary strategy for this use case
Explains that blue-green with header-based preview allows testing before ANY real traffic exposure
Explains why canary is riskier here: even 5% weight means 5% of payment transactions hit unvalidated code
Mentions prePromotionAnalysis for automated validation of the preview before promotion
Acknowledges the trade-off: blue-green uses 2x resources (both versions run simultaneously)
Does NOT just describe both strategies — makes a clear recommendation with reasoning specific to the payments/financial context
Mentions that after blue-green promotion, the old version can be kept as instant rollback

evals.name: Diagnose 503s after enabling strict mTLS
evals.prompt: We just enabled strict mTLS across the cluster with a mesh-wide PeerAuthentication in istio-system. Now our legacy monitoring stack (Prometheus scraping /metrics endpoints from application pods) is getting 503 errors from all services in the mesh. The monitoring namespace 'openshift-monitoring' does NOT have sidecar injection enabled. The Prometheus pods don't have Istio sidecars. What's happening and how do we fix it without disabling mTLS for the whole cluster?
expectations: Correctly identifies root cause: Prometheus without a sidecar cannot present a client TLS certificate, so mTLS-enforced services reject the connection with 503
Does NOT recommend disabling strict mTLS cluster-wide (that would defeat the purpose)
Offers multiple fix options with trade-offs
Option 1: Enable sidecar injection in the monitoring namespace (most secure but may conflict with openshift-monitoring)
Option 2: Create a per-port PeerAuthentication in PERMISSIVE mode for the metrics port only (targeted exception)
Option 3: Use Istio's built-in Prometheus metrics merge or envoy stats endpoint as an alternative scrape source
Recommends the least-privilege fix (per-port PERMISSIVE or metrics endpoint) over broad namespace exceptions
Provides the actual PeerAuthentication YAML for the recommended fix

evals.name: Red herring: 503s that look like mTLS but aren't
evals.prompt:
We're getting 503 errors on our checkout-svc after a deployment. We recently enabled strict mTLS, so we assumed that's the cause. But we checked — the checkout namespace HAS sidecar injection enabled, all pods have sidecars, and PeerAuthentication is STRICT everywhere. The 503s only happen when traffic comes from the payments-svc to checkout-svc. Traffic from the frontend to checkout-svc works fine.

Here's our DestinationRule:
  apiVersion: networking.istio.io/v1
  kind: DestinationRule
  metadata:
    name: checkout-svc-dr
    namespace: checkout
  spec:
    host: checkout-svc
    subsets:
      - name: stable
        labels:
          version: v2
      - name: canary
        labels:
          version: v3

And our VirtualService routes all traffic to the 'stable' subset. But our checkout-svc pods have the label app: checkout-svc and NO 'version' label at all.

Why are we getting 503s?
expectations: Does NOT blame mTLS — correctly identifies that mTLS is configured properly (both sides have sidecars, STRICT is fine)
Identifies the real root cause: DestinationRule subset labels (version: v2) don't match the pod labels (pods have no 'version' label)
Explains that Istio routes to an empty subset when labels don't match, returning 503
Explains why traffic from frontend works but payments doesn't — if frontend doesn't use a DestinationRule or routes to the host directly without subset selection
Recommends fixing the pod labels to include version: v2, OR updating the DestinationRule subset labels to match existing pod labels
Does NOT recommend changing PeerAuthentication or mTLS settings — that's the red herring

evals.name: Conflicting requirements: strict mTLS + external non-TLS service
evals.prompt: We need to call an external payment processor API at http://legacy-processor.partner.com:8080 (plain HTTP, no TLS — they're a legacy partner and won't upgrade). We also have a strict company policy: all service-to-service communication must use mTLS, enforced by a mesh-wide PeerAuthentication in STRICT mode. Our payments-svc in the mesh needs to call this external endpoint. How do I make this work without weakening our mTLS policy?
expectations: Identifies the fundamental conflict: STRICT mTLS applies to sidecar-proxied traffic, but the external service is outside the mesh
Explains that Istio's mTLS policy only applies to traffic between sidecars — traffic to external services uses ServiceEntry + DestinationRule, not PeerAuthentication
Recommends creating a ServiceEntry for the external endpoint
Recommends a DestinationRule for the external host with tls.mode: DISABLE (since the partner doesn't support TLS)

Addresses the security concern: suggests compensating controls (egress gateway for audit logging, NetworkPolicy to restrict which pods can reach the external service, AuthorizationPolicy to limit which ServiceAccounts can call it)
Does NOT recommend weakening the mesh-wide STRICT PeerAuthentication
Does NOT claim this is impossible — Istio handles mesh-internal and mesh-external traffic differently
Provides actual ServiceEntry and DestinationRule YAML
